subject.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup

question: Which process boundary should own macOS/BSD mount classification before SQLite databases are opened?
rationale: Removing the synchronous probe may conservatively disable WAL on otherwise-local filesystems, while retaining it permits user-visible startup stalls; choosing the permanent classification boundary requires SQLite owner intent.

options.title: Prepare classification asynchronously
options.body: Classify the relevant filesystem once before database initialization, cache the process-stable result, and pass or reuse it for each database open.

options.title: Fail conservative without probing
options.body: Remove the external command from database open and select rollback journaling whenever statfs or proc metadata cannot classify the filesystem.

options.title: Accept the bounded stall
options.body: Keep the one-second synchronous timeout only with explicit owner acceptance and supported-host proof covering repeated database opens.

recommendation.title: Prepare classification asynchronously
recommendation.body: Classify the relevant filesystem once before database initialization, cache the process-stable result, and pass or reuse it for each database open.
